page_checks.summary: Negation scope produces two readings with all, and none combines negative and existential meaning. Postverbal some may take wide scope.
Existential any is non-affirmative, questions can favor some or any differently, and plural some differs from any and none in minimum quantity.
The quantifier table separates neutral and dual forms. Only both is limited to binary coordination, and questions can permit free-choice readings.
Free choice need not require all members. Each and every mark distributivity, and universal quantification typically presupposes existence.
Universals can occur without asserting existence. Cardinal bounds distinguish entailment from a defeasible exact-number inference.
Scalar inference extends to proportional some. Partitives force a relevant set, while nonproportional unstressed some need not invoke one.
Proportional and superlative most differ. The positive scale contrasts all, most, and some, with a separate account of multal quantities.
High quantities and low quantities participate in distinct scales. Negative quantifiers assert restrictions that positive items may merely suggest.
The negative proportional scale and the a few versus few table distinguish asserted from cancellable upper and lower bounds.
The definite article signals contextual identifiability with singular, plural, and mass nouns. A unique description can suffice without familiarity.
Singular uniqueness admits contextual flexibility. Existence presupposition projects under negation, while plural and mass definites target a maximal whole.
Definite totality can be weaker than universality. Sensory context, shared knowledge, prior mention, and association license definites.
Modifiers and predication can establish identifiability. Stressed and comparative the are distinguished from fused-head constructions. Indefinite a is introduced.
Quantitative and nonquantitative a differ. Initial a is excluded in the cited attributive numeral and genitive configurations.
Noninitial a can remain in an attributive modifier. Demonstratives add deixis or anaphora and occur in fused-head and degree uses.
Personal determinatives and pronoun apposition differ in constituency and case. Dual both and size-neutral all are introduced.
All and both differ in countability, modification, and compatibility with indefinite expressions. Whole contrasts in its distribution and agreement preferences.
All and both can act as determiners or predeterminers and head partitive fusions. All also participates in special fused-head expressions.
Informal the both of us is restricted. Modifier all and coordination marker both differ, as do distributive and joint readings.
Reciprocal properties can occur with all and both. Each typically ranges over an identifiable set, while every also permits generic readings.
Each and every contrast in degree, modification, fused heads, postgenitive placement, compounds, and preferred set size.
Some exhibits basic, considerable-quantity, and vague singular uses, alongside its contrast with non-affirmative any.
Exclamatory and proportional some differ from basic nonproportional some. Existential any allows some singular count heads.
Existential any has countability, stress, and polarity distinctions. Free-choice any licenses arbitrary selection across three head types.
